answers.In a sentence or two, what will it do fo: It summarises last month's internal ticket volumes from our own reporting database into a written summary for the operations team.
answers.Where does the AI come from?: Something a team in your firm built for this job
answers.What kind of AI is it? If more than one: Reads, summarises, translates, writes or answers questions in words
What information will it see or use? Tic: Confidential firm information — internal data, code or documents not meant for outside the firm, whether or not they’re marked confidential
answers.What happens with what it produces? If i: finds or summarises for people to read — nobody acts on it directly
answers.Who ends up seeing or receiving what it: Only me or my own team
answers.Which of these does it help decide, if a: None of these — it’s for day-to-day work
answers.How widely will it be used?: My team, as part of normal work

didntUnderstand.where: Nudge screen, 'We found no words about:' list
didntUnderstand.quote: Who ends up receiving what it produces / What information it will see or use — 'no words found'
didntUnderstand.why: I wrote 'for the operations team' and 'reads from our own reporting database', so it looks like I did cover who receives it and what it reads. I don't understand why it says it found no words. It makes me doubt whether the tool read my sentence properly. The form then pre-fills 'Only me or my own team' from 'for the operations team', which contradicts the nudge.

didntUnderstand.quote: What your description mentions … 'This only notes which topics your words touch.'
didntUnderstand.why: I can follow that it is just a keyword check. I don't see what I should do with it, or whether a missing tick is a problem.

didntUnderstand.quote: AI helper alpha:7b: not yet tested on the example cases
didntUnderstand.why: 'alpha:7b' means nothing to me, and I don't know what 'the example cases' are or why 'not tested' matters for my answers.

didntUnderstand.quote: Setup steps for whoever runs Ollama
didntUnderstand.why: I don't know what Ollama is. The text says I needn't do anything, so I skipped it.

didntUnderstand.quote: 2 Similar checks (shown as '← Similar checks') / 3 Your answers / 4 Questions
didntUnderstand.why: I don't know what 'Similar checks' are or why it has a back arrow. I also can't tell the difference between 'Your answers' (the screen I'm on) and 'Questions' (the next step).
Nearly everything is pick-from-a-list. Only the name and one-sentence boxes take my own words.

didntUnderstand.where: Form: Where does the AI come from?
didntUnderstand.quote: Where does the AI come from? / Something a team in your firm built for this job
didntUnderstand.why: I built the dashboard, but I'm not sure which AI model writes the summary or who supplies it. I picked 'built for this job' but can't be sure it's right.

didntUnderstand.where: Form: What kind of AI is it?
didntUnderstand.quote: pick the one nearest the bottom of this list
didntUnderstand.why: 'Nearest the bottom' would be 'Not sure', which can't be what is meant. It is unclear whether it means the most capable or the last one that fits.

didntUnderstand.quote: Could the people who built it show you why it gave a particular result? / 'which factors drove each result'
didntUnderstand.why: It is unclear what the 'result' of a summary tool is, and what 'factors' would be. I can show where the numbers come from, but not why the AI worded a sentence the way it did, so I guessed 'No, or I don’t know'.

didntUnderstand.where: Form: pre-fill for What happens with what it produces
didntUnderstand.why: I ticked it, but 'directly' is a stretch: people in the operations team will read the summary and may act on it. I took it to mean nothing happens automatically.

didntUnderstand.where: Form: Which countries does it involve?
didntUnderstand.why: I understand the question, but it isn't obvious why an internal ticket summary would involve a country. Nothing I typed says where my firm is based, so I chose 'Somewhere else, or not sure'.

expectNext: Pressing Continue should check that every question has an answer and every suggestion has been ticked or changed. If something is missing it should stop me and say what. If all is complete, I expect it to move to the next step, 'Questions', which may ask a few more things about my dashboard. Then a 'Confirm' page should show my answers back to me, and a 'Result' page should say whether I can go ahead and what needs doing first. I expect that to be decided by checking my answers against the firm's written rules, so the same answers always give the same result, with no AI making the decision.
ticksMean: 'I've checked this answer' means I have read the AI helper's suggested answer next to my own words and I agree it is right. It is my confirmation, not the helper's. Until I tick it (or change the answer), the suggestion doesn't count and I can't continue. Changing the answer also counts as having checked it. The helper only suggests; I am the one vouching for the answer.
comment: As an operations analyst I could finish the form, but I got stuck on the nudge saying 'no words found' about who receives it and what it reads when I had written both, and on the unexplained jargon (alpha:7b, Ollama, 'Similar checks'). I also guessed on the countries and 'built for this job' answers.
